new_sources.summary: This project examined creative techniques of characterisation and musical specialist language to create a modern classical musician character constructed from a musician’s experiences rather than generic tropes often found in fiction. Practice-led research and a reflective framework applied to the author’s musicianship informed three short stories of speculative fiction, while literary code-switching techniques facilitated the inclusion of musical language. Therefore, this project attempted to bridge the gap between the musician experience and fictional representation in a way that is consonant with a musician’s experience of musicianship.

new_sources.summary: Conventional music representations describe acoustic energy over time and frequency but do not explicitly expose relations among simultaneous frequency components. We introduce the \emph{Dissonance Spectrum} (DS), a nonnegative time--frequency representation that applies a tolerance-based rational pitch-relation kernel with logarithmic harmonic distance to a constant-Q spectrum and attributes aggregate pairwise interactions back to individual frequency bins. Controlled music-theory tests show strong ordinal agreement for intervals, harmonic-function connections, and church modes, and weaker but significant agreement across diverse chord voicings. DS is then encoded by a lightweight parallel
new_sources.title: Dissonance Spectrum explicitly models perceptual frequency interactions for better music understanding
